title: Vertical Stabiliser — Installation of Bonding Straps at the Fin Box Rib Feet
abstract: Installation of woven bonding straps between the fin box rib feet and the spar, with an extension of the skin conductive mesh, so that a lightning attachment is carried through the joint rather than across it.

sections.planning_reason: Three lightning strike investigations found pitting and localised delamination at the fin box rib feet rather than at the attachment point, which shows that the current is jumping the joint. In-service measurement on twenty aircraft found joint resistance rising with age as the sealant ages and the faying surfaces oxidise. None of the events affected controllability but each one required a composite repair with the aircraft on ground.
sections.description: The conductive mesh in the fin box skin is extended aft to overlap the rib feet, and a woven bonding strap kit D5530119137814 is installed between each rib foot and the spar. The forward shear tie D5530110749890 is retained and re-drilled so that the strap terminates on a dedicated fastener. The gusset kit SAD726961-22 at the lower rib positions is replaced by an item with an integral conductive land. Countersunk screws AES932279K1 attach the strap, with protective sleeving LN606161K1 where it crosses an edge.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Open the fin box access panels and put lighting and ventilation into the box. Measure and record the bonding resistance at every rib foot before any work is done. Clean the faying surfaces at the rib feet back to bare material and mask the surrounding laminate. Apply the conductive mesh extension patches to the skin, working aft from the existing mesh boundary, and cure to the schedule in the accomplishment instructions. Replace the gusset kit SAD726961-22 at the lower rib positions with the conductive land item. Drill the dedicated strap fastener into the shear tie D5530110749890 using the position jig and deburr. Install the bonding strap kit D5530119137814 at each rib foot with countersunk screws AES932279K1, fitting protective sleeving LN606161K1 at every edge crossing. Measure the bonding resistance again and confirm that every path is inside the limit. Restore the surface protection and close the access panels. Do the fin box bonding check of AMM-T-55-30-11-200-003-A and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to TITAN-88 aircraft up to and including MSN T00155. Aircraft from MSN T00156 onwards were built with the extended mesh and the strap installation. The rudder does not have to be removed. Aircraft carrying an approved composite repair inside the fin box must be assessed by Aeralis before accomplishment.
sections.material_note: Kit K5530-1009-01 covers one aircraft and contains the straps, the mesh patches, the gusset kits and all bonding hardware. Kit lead time is twenty-four weeks. The mesh patch adhesive has a six-month shelf life from despatch and must be stored below five degrees.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled base maintenance visit, or within 72 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.
